title: 橘直幹、兼官を望み申文を書く
gendaibun: 村上天皇のころ、文章博士の橘直幹は詩文にすぐれながら家は貧しく、子だくさんの暮らしを支えるため民部大輔の兼官を願い、みずから申文を書いた。
kobun: 村上天皇の御時、<ruby><rb>長門守</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>ながとのかみ</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>長盛が子にて、<ruby><rb>文章</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>もんじょう</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>博士、<ruby><rb>橘直幹</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>たちばななおもと</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>といふ儒者ありけり。風月に巧みなりけれども、官は凄まじく、文章には富めりしかども、家は貧しくして、<ruby><rb>顔淵</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>がんえん</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>が巷にをなじく、<ruby><rb>閨</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>ねや</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>は雨漏りて、<ruby><rb>原憲</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>げんけん</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>が<ruby><rb>枢</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>とぼそ</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>にかはらざりけり。僅かに<ruby><rb>民部大輔</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>みんぶのたいふ</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>を望み申すとて、みづから<ruby><rb>申文</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>もうしぶみ</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>をぞ書きける。
desc: 絵は直幹の邸とその近隣を描く。子らが遊ぶ室内、雨漏りじみた家屋、市場や小社のある町並みと続き、申文を草する動機である窮乏と家族の多さが視覚化される。詞書は顔淵の陋巷・原憲の蓬戸に喩えて、才学と貧困の落差を強調する。
gendaibunen: In the reign of Emperor Murakami, the scholar Tachibana no Naomoto excelled at poetry yet lived in poverty. To support his large household he sought a concurrent post as Minbu no Taifu and wrote a petition himself.
kobunen: In the reign of Emperor Murakami there lived a Confucian scholar named Tachibana no Naomoto, son of Nagamori, Governor of Nagato, and a Doctor of Letters. Though skilled in poetry and rich in learning, his household was poor—like Yan Yuan's humble lane, his rooms leaked like Yuan Xian's door. Hoping for the concurrent post of Minbu no Taifu, he wrote a petition himself.
descen: The paintings show Naomoto's house and neighborhood—children at home, a worn dwelling, a market and a small shrine—making visible the poverty that drives his petition. The caption likens his hardship to classical Chinese exemplars of scholarly poverty.
titleen: Naomoto drafts a petition for concurrent office

title: 直幹の申文に、村上天皇機嫌を損ずる
gendaibun: 直幹は申文を小野道風に清書させ、職事を通じて奏聞した。帝がみずから開くと「人によりて事異なり」などの文言で機嫌を損じ、廷臣たちは恐れた。
kobun: この申文を小野道風に清書を誂へて、<ruby><rb>職事</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>しきじ</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>に付けて奏聞したりければ、御門（帝）心憎くしや思し召しけん。御手づから取りて開き御覧ぜられける程に、「人に依りて事異なり」と書ける所に至りて、申文を差し置かせ賜（→給）ひて、<ruby><rb>天気快</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>てけこころよ</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>からざりければ、人々<ruby><rb>懼</rb><rp>（</rp><rt>おそ</rt><rp>）</rp></ruby>れ思ひけり
desc: 詞書は清書と奏聞、帝の不快を述べる。絵はその後の参内準備として、建物前の官人から牛車に乗る場面へ進む。文言の直截さが、兼官格差への苦情として帝の怒りを招いたと読める。
gendaibunen: Naomoto had Ono no Michikaze fair-copy the petition and submitted it through a court secretary. When the Emperor opened it himself, wording such as “things differ by the person” offended him, and the courtiers were afraid.
kobunen: He had Ono no Michikaze make a fair copy and presented it through a shikiji (secretary). The Emperor, uneasy, took it up himself; when he reached the line “things differ depending on the person,” he set the petition aside. His mood darkened, and those present grew fearful.
descen: The caption covers the fair copy, presentation, and the Emperor's anger. Paintings then show officials and boarding an ox cart for court. The blunt wording about unequal favor is what spoils the imperial mood.
titleen: Emperor Murakami is offended by the petition

title: 愁訴の情を書き連ねる直幹の申文
gendaibun: 申文は、直幹が両官を停止された例のない処遇と、三統元夏が少輔を兼ねた先例とを対比し、七年ひとりの職を守ってきた窮状を訴える。
kobun: 彼申文に、「直幹謹案内をかんがうるに、去天暦二年、大学頭大内記より当職に排せし日、所帯の両官、みな停止せらる。朝家に文章博士をはじめをかれてよりのち、いまだその例をきかず。又、同四年にいた（り脱力）て、三儀（統）元夏式部小輔より儒職に除せし日、少輔をやめずして、「兼」の字をたまはる。拝除の息（恩）これ一なれども、栄枯の分をなじからず。人によて事ことなり。偏頗ににたりといへども、天にかはて官をさづく、まことに運命にかかれり。独一職をまもりて、爰七年をへたり」など、さまざまに書てたてまつりけるとなむ。
desc: 詞書は申文本文を引用し、第二段で帝が不快とした根拠を示す。絵は朱雀大路の牛車道中から朱塗りの殿舎、廷臣の座、右大将実頼のラベルへと進み、宮廷空間へ入る。
gendaibunen: The petition contrasts Naomoto’s unprecedented loss of both prior posts with Mimune no Motonatsu’s concurrent office as Junior Assistant, pleading the hardship of holding a single post for seven years.
kobunen: That petition said, in sum: “Naomoto humbly considers precedent. In Tenryaku 2, on the day he was appointed from Head of the University and Senior Secretary to his present post, both offices he held were stopped—unheard of since Doctors of Letters were first instituted. In Tenryaku 4, when Mimune no Motonatsu moved from Junior Assistant of Ceremonial to a Confucian post, he kept the assistantship and received the character ‘concurrent.’ Imperial favor is one, yet fortune differs; things differ by the person. Though it may seem partial, office is granted in Heaven’s stead and hangs on destiny. I have guarded a single post these seven years”—and so he wrote at length.
descen: The caption quotes the petition, revealing why the Emperor took offense. Paintings follow the ox cart along the avenue into red palace halls and courtiers, including a figure labeled Fujiwara no Saneyori.

title: 内裏炎上に際し、帝、直幹の申文の安否を問う
gendaibun: 天徳四年九月二十三日子刻、内裏が炎上する。帝は中院へ渡り重宝の搬出を見たのち、「直幹が申文は取り出したや」と問うた。
kobun: 俄中院に御ゆきなりたりけるに、朝々代々の御わたりもの、御椅子・時簡・玄象・鈴鹿以下、もちて参たりけるに、叡覧ありて、「直幹が申文はとりいでたや」と仰ありけるにこそ。先日奏覧の時、御気色あしかりしかば、人々をそれたりしに、今御尋こそいみじけれとて、よの人ありがたき事になん申あひたりける。其時のことぞかし、火は左衛門の陣よりいできたれば、内侍所のおはします温明殿もほどちかかりけるうへ、如法夜中の事なりしかば、内侍も女官も参あはずして、賢所をもいだしたてまつらず。少（小）野宮殿、いそぎまいり賜（給）て、内侍所をみたてまつらせたまうにわたらせ給はず。世は今はかうにこそありけれとおぼして、御なみだをながさせ給ける程に、南殿のさくらの木のこずえに御かがみかからせ給へり。光明奕棘として、朝の日の山をいづるがごとし。世はいまだうせざりけりとおぼしける。感涙をさへがたくて、右の御膝をつきて、左の御袖をひろげて申させ賜けるは、「昔天照御神百王をまぶりたてまつらむと御ちかひありけり。そのむねあらたまらずば、神鏡実頼がそでにやどり給へ」と申給ける。御詞いまだをはらざるにとびいり賜へり。御袖につつみて大政官の朝所へぞわたしたてまつられける。この世にはうけたてまつらんと思よる人もありがたく、御鏡も入給まじ。上代こそめでたく侍けれ。抑皇居には、難波・藤原の両館はむかしの事也。此京に遷都ののちは、これぞはじめにて侍ける。
desc: 詞書は大火の夜、帝が申文の安否を尋ねたこと、左衛門の陣から出火し温明殿の神鏡を出せなかったこと、小野宮実頼が紫宸殿の左近桜に神鏡を見出した奇瑞を語る。絵は避難の牛車・騎馬、煙と炎に包まれる殿舎を描き、巻末に安政四年写了の識語がある。
gendaibunen: At midnight on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of Tentoku 4, fire broke out in the palace. After moving to the Chūin residence and seeing treasures carried out, the Emperor asked, “Was Naomoto’s petition brought out?”
kobunen: When the Emperor hastily moved to the Chūin, heirlooms of successive reigns—the imperial chair, the hour plaques, the biwa Genjō and Suzuka, and more—were brought before him. He asked, “Was Naomoto’s petition taken out?” Though his mood had been dark when it was first presented, people now marvelled that he inquired after it. The fire had begun at the Left Gate Guards’ post; the Unmei-den housing the Naishidokoro was nearby, and at midnight no attendants came, so the sacred mirror was not carried out. Lord Onomiya (Fujiwara no Saneyori) hurried there, found it gone, and wept—then saw the mirror hanging in the cherry tree of the Southern Hall, bright as the morning sun over the mountains. Kneeling, he spread his left sleeve and prayed that if Amaterasu’s vow to protect a hundred sovereigns still held, the mirror would lodge in his sleeve; before he finished, it flew in. He wrapped it and bore it to the morning hall of the Council of State. Few in later ages would dare receive it so; such wonders belong to antiquity. After the move to this capital, this was said to be the first great palace fire—Naniwa and Fujiwara halls being of old.
descen: The caption recounts the Tentoku 4 fire, the Emperor asking after Naomoto's petition, and Saneyori finding the sacred mirror on the Sakon cherry. Paintings show flight and flames; a colophon dated Ansei 4 marks the copy at the end.
titleen: Palace fire; the Emperor asks after the petition
